clue.text: For whom something finally turned up in Australia

definitions.text: For whom something finally turned up in Australia

parts.words: For whom something finally turned up in Australia
parts.note: Dickens's ever-hopeful debtor in David Copperfield kept waiting for something to turn up, and found success only after emigrating to Australia

explanation.surface: A question about someone whose luck changed at last down under.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at the David Copperfield character famous for saying something will turn up; Dickens ends his story with the man prospering as a magistrate in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens optimist's catchphrase was that something would turn up, and his fortune finally came in the colony.

clue.text: One comparatively blind spot?

definitions.meaning: a burrowing animal with tiny eyes and poor sight
a small dark mark on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The burrowing animal is proverbially blind, and the same word is a dark skin mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The burrowing mammal has very weak eyesight, and the same word names a dark blemish on the skin.

clue.text: Bible translator is a common fellow, poor dear-—about fifty

parts.note: cove is old slang for a fellow

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other piece
poor means the word dear is in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Bible translator is described as an ordinary chap, poor dear, about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' scrambles DEAR to RDAE, and 'about' sets it round L to make RDALE after COVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Coverdale produced the first complete printed English Bible in 1535.

clue.text: Sin, as Omar's paradise-substitute ?

parts.note: Sin is a desert, and in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam a desert place with wine and a loved one were paradise enough

explanation.surface: Wickedness offered as the poet's replacement for heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Sin is the biblical desert (the Wilderness of Sin), not wrongdoing; FitzGerald's Omar says a desert place with bread, wine and 'thou' were paradise enow.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert region, like the biblical one of Sin, which Omar's verse ranks as paradise.

clue.text: Poet gives up work under direction

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole is read from the bottom upwards
in a down clue the direction is written below the work

parts.note: toil is work
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A poet abandons work because of management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives up' looks like quitting, but in a down entry it turns TOILE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, was a major modernist poet.

clue.text: Plan to get round his awkward accident

indicators.note: the plan's letters go round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a map is a plan, as of a town

indicators.note: awkward means the word his is clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's scheme to work around a clumsy man ends in a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles HIS to ISH, and 'to get round' puts MAP around it: M-ISH-AP.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor unlucky accident or misadventure is a synonym.

clue.text: Complaints of breathless ascents

indicators.note: the letter H stands for a breath, so without breath the H goes

parts.note: hills are ascents

explanation.surface: Grumbles about climbs that leave you puffed.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the aspirate, a breath sound, so 'breathless' drops it from HILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments or troubles are synonyms, as in the ills of old age.

clue.text: Water carrier meets a prophet

parts.note: a hose carries water

explanation.surface: A man with a pitcher runs into a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor prophet of the Old Testament who has a book named after him.

clue.text: Perhaps the end

parts.note: a note added after the signature comes at the very end of a letter

explanation.surface: Possibly the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The PS added after a letter's signature is perhaps its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A note added after a letter is signed sits at its close.

clue.text: Girl appears to scoff about backward European

indicators.note: the scoffing word goes round the turned letters

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff

indicators.note: the European's letters are turned round

parts.note: a Finn is a European

explanation.surface: A girl seems to mock a slow-witted European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like slow-witted but turns FINN into NNIF, which 'about' puts in JEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as for any girl.

clue.text: French politician is returned — no change

indicators.note: reading the name back from its end gives no change at all, so the letters form a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A French politician comes back to office and nothing is different.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Laval was a French prime minister of the 1930s and Vichy era; 'returned — no change' says his name reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Laval was a French premier and Vichy collaborator, so a politician from France.

clue.text: Thought is mainly inclined to make them visionaries

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship on the main (the sea) that is inclined to one side lists

explanation.surface: Someone whose thinking leans a certain way counts as a dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' is the trick: the main is the open sea, and a ship that is inclined there lists.
explanation.definitionFit: People who pursue lofty principles and perfect visions of the world are dreamers or visionaries.

clue.text: Most economical builder ?

parts.note: read as a superlative, free is the most economical price; a builder here is a material for building, a fine-grained stone that can be cut in any direction

explanation.surface: A question about which tradesman charges least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'builder' looks like a tradesman but is building material: a sandstone or limestone that cuts freely, whose first part also means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-grained stone easily worked in any direction, used for building, whose name begins with a word for costing nothing.

clue.text: Proceed as in 8

indicators.note: the word as is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: 8 down is a postscript, abbreviated PS

explanation.surface: An instruction to carry on as in a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as in 8' is literal: AS goes in PS, the short form of the answer to 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on or move along is a synonym, as when traffic is told to go by.

clue.text: Wondered if Bob was an embezzler

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S
to peculate is to embezzle

explanation.surface: Someone wondered whether a man called Bob had been stealing funds.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is not a name but old British slang for a shilling, abbreviated s in pounds, shillings and pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Mused or guessed about something without firm knowledge.

clue.text: Bound to arrange retirement in time

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring

indicators.note: the word retires, going backwards

parts.note: to edit is to arrange text

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to sort out retiring in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' means drawing back, turning EDIT to TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for the spring season, a time of year.

clue.text: He brings action into a simple quarrel

parts.note: plain means simple
a tiff is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone drags a petty squabble into court.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit or legal action against another is the claimant in court.

clue.text: Tip diner changed, being brave

indicators.note: changed means the letters of tip diner are altered in order

explanation.surface: A diner changes how much to tip, which takes courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and bold, a synonym for brave.

clue.text: Old-fashioned pop writer

definitions.meaning: a dated, schoolboy Latin word for father, pop being dad

explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is a father, not music; the Latin word for father was old public-school slang for dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for father was old-fashioned British slang for dad, and Walter Pater was a Victorian essayist.

clue.text: Supporter of steps taken at high level

definitions.text: Supporter of steps taken at high level

parts.words: Supporter of steps taken at high level
parts.note: a circus funambulist's steps are taken high up on a taut cord that holds them up

explanation.surface: A backer of policies made at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps taken at high level' sounds like government policy but means footsteps on a high wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut rope high above the circus floor bears an acrobat walking along it.

clue.text: Letter written after church board meeting

indicators.note: the letter's name is put after the church abbreviation

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A letter is drafted after a church board meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' is not a committee but two players meeting over a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played on a board where two opponents meet is the board game of kings and pawns.

clue.text: Happening to be the last thing in treatment of toes

definitions.text: to be the last thing in treatment of toes
definitions.meaning: to point one's toes skyward is the idiom for dying, the last thing a person does

explanation.walkthrough: To 'turn up one's toes' is British slang for dying, hence the last thing done with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving or occurring is one sense; the idiom of toes pointing skyward means dying.

clue.text: Minor characters in Miles Standish

indicators.note: the letters (characters) sit inside the words Miles Standish

explanation.surface: Bit-part players in a story about the Pilgrim captain Miles Standish.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles Standish was a Mayflower Pilgrim leader and subject of a Longfellow poem; 'Minor characters' looks like bit parts but 'characters in' signals letters within.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor and smaller in amount or degree are synonyms, as in a lesser sum.

clue.text: Little Pole takes hammer

parts.note: S is the South Pole
a mall is an old word for a heavy hammer or mallet

explanation.surface: A small Polish man picks up a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is the South Pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and little are synonyms.

clue.text: Prize for putting 501 in prison

indicators.note: the numerals are put inside the prison's name

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious old London prison
in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1

explanation.surface: A prisoner is jailed for 501 days for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Newdigate Prize is Oxford University's poetry prize; Newgate was a famous London jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford University award for English verse is named after Sir Roger Newdigate.

clue.text: Why he's capped, he hasn't a clue

definitions.text: Why he's capped, he hasn't a clue

parts.words: Why he's capped, he hasn't a clue
parts.note: a slow pupil made to wear a pointed cap because he knows nothing

explanation.surface: A sportsman picked for his country has no idea why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capped' suggests a sports cap, but this is the pointed cap put on a slow schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow learner, once made to wear a conical cap in class.

clue.text: Entry permit by way of South interior

indicators.note: South goes in the interior of the other word

parts.note: via means by way of

explanation.surface: A permit to enter via the southern interior.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp in a passport allowing entry into a country.

clue.text: Island supplies sound crew

indicators.note: sound says the word for the crew is spoken, giving the island's name

parts.note: a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is an eight

explanation.surface: An island provides a healthy crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but it signals a homophone; an eyot is a small river island, as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in a river, a Thames term.

clue.text: Exit criminal to where there's no ex-it---an old custom ?

indicators.note: the clue says ex is absent, so those letters are removed from the front

parts.note: sending a criminal out of the country is extradition

explanation.surface: A convict leaves for a place with no way out, following old practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ex-it' splits the word exit to name the letters EX, which 'there's no' removes from the front of EXTRADITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-established custom or belief handed down through generations.

clue.text: Jumbo output is highly valued

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, so its output is the tusk material, prized and costly

explanation.surface: A large production is much prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like an adjective for big, but it is the name for an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusks yield a precious white material long prized for carving.

clue.text: Jacket for a crazy old man

indicators.note: crazy means the word old is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coat suited to an eccentric elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles OLD to DOL, then MAN follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar's jacket worn slung over one shoulder, or a woman's cape-like coat.

clue.text: In principle people employed in building

indicators.note: the workers are placed inside the principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle
men are workers, people employed

explanation.surface: In principle, workers are employed on the construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' reads as a phrase meaning theoretically, but 'In' puts MEN inside TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building divided into flats or rooms let to separate households.
